newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends steady to up, cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends steady to up, cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended unchanged to higher Friday in moderate trade, with a steady weekend cash market underpinning the complex though prices held in recent technical ranges, industry sources said.
March edged up 1.4 cents to close at $1.936 per million British thermal units. April settled 0.8 cent higher at $1.919. Other months ended steady to up one cent.

"We opened weak this morning but couldn't break down, so we moved back up on short covering. When we couldn't get above $1.95, we were stuck in a range," said a Midwest trader, adding mild weather later next week could keep prices soft.

Despite a couple of days of cold, traders said forecasts for mostly normal to above-normal U.S. temperatures into early March could set a bearish tone during bidweek next week and make any paper rally difficult to sustain.
"I think cash buyers may back away next week," the trader said.
And while some technical traders were looking for a short covering bounce, few expected much upside.
"I need to see an April close above $2.04 to get interested," said a Houston-based trader.
Resistance in April was seen at $1.985, then at $2.04 and $2.16. April support was pegged at $1.87, then at $1.845, with additional buying likely at the contract low of $1.701.
For March, which expires Monday, chartists still saw support at Tuesday's low of $1.85 and then at the contract low of $1.749. Resistance was at $2.08-2.09 and then $2.25-2.30.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend prices were pegged little changed Friday at about $1.90. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-to-mid $1.70s. New York city gate weekend gas was down slightly to the $2.10-15 area.
The 12-month strip rose 0.4 cent to $2.056. NYMEX said an estimated 47,262 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 58,298.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Friday.

On the KCBT, March finished one cent higher at $1.65, while deferreds ended steady to up one cent. The East/West spread widened by 0.4 cent to 28.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 220 lots changed hands, down sharply from Thursday's total of 548.
